title: Business plan written (31 Oct 2026)
Research: which games can legally be used commercially
Research: ADIPS process and registered inspection bodies
Research: specialist insurance brokers
Launch checklist written (Docs + PDF)
ADIPS inspection request email drafted
Insurance quote request email drafted (5-point harness confirmed)
Operations manual draft written (11 sections + 3 appendices; Docs + PDF)
Emails pack PDF (both emails + recipients)
Send ADIPS email to Rundle, TÜV SÜD, Westlakes
why: Ride safety inspectors get booked up weeks ahead. Asking now means we can get an inspection date in time.
notes: Confirm with Sam whether already sent.

title: Send insurance email to Broker2U, Acer, Peacock and Skysmart's broker; ask for quotes by about 14 Nov
why: We can't sell vouchers without public liability insurance, and quotes take a week or two to come back.
notes: Confirm with Sam whether already sent.

title: Decide with Andy: SmartMotion as a Skysmart division or a new Ltd
why: Decides whose name goes on the insurance, contracts, bank account and invoices. A lot of the other paperwork depends on it.

title: Check the "SmartMotion" name and trademark (UK IPO)
why: Makes sure nobody else already owns the SmartMotion name before we spend money on signs, the website and marketing.

title: Accountant: VAT position; separate bank account or cost centre
why: Tells us whether our prices have to include VAT, and keeps SmartMotion's money separate from Skysmart's.

title: Landlord consent and planning-use check for public visitors
why: The landlord and the council need to be happy with members of the public visiting the unit.

title: Licence requests: Eagle Dynamics, Assetto Corsa reseller, FlyPT Mover developer; buy X-Plane Pro
why: Normal copies of games can't legally be used for paid rides. Each software company has to give commercial permission, and some take time to reply.

title: Compare insurance quotes; bind public liability cover
why: Pick the best quote and buy the cover. This is a must-have before any vouchers are sold.

title: Choose and book the ADIPS inspection body
why: Pick an inspector and get a date in the diary. Event organisers will ask for their certificate.

title: Written risk assessment (base + event template)
why: A written list of what could go wrong and how we stop it happening. Inspectors and insurers will ask to see it.

title: Complete the operations manual [bracketed] values with rig data
why: The operations manual has blanks (like maximum rider weight) that need the rig's real measurements.

title: Set rider restrictions (age, height, weight, medical)
why: Who can and can't ride: minimum age and height, maximum weight, and health conditions.

title: Gentle, Medium and Strong motion profiles per title
why: Three comfort levels for each experience, so nervous first-timers and thrill-seekers both enjoy it.

title: PAT testing of all electrical kit
why: Every plug-in electrical item gets a safety test and a sticker. Insurers and events expect it.

title: Sign at least one flight and one car commercial licence
why: We need at least one flight game and one driving game with a signed commercial licence before we sell anything.

title: Choose booking system (Bookeo / Checkfront)
why: The online system where customers choose a time slot and pay.

title: Set up vouchers: unique codes, 12-month expiry, redemption tracking
why: Gift vouchers need their own codes, an expiry date, and a way to mark them as used.

title: Card payments set up and tested (Stripe / Square / SumUp)
why: Taking card payments online and in person. Do a real test purchase to prove it works.

title: Health and eligibility questions in booking flow
why: Customers answer health and eligibility questions when they book, so anyone unsuitable is spotted before they turn up.

title: Booking and voucher terms (solicitor check)
why: The small print for bookings and vouchers: refunds, cancellations and expiry. A solicitor should check it.

title: Rider declaration and parental consent form
why: The form every rider signs before riding, plus a version for parents of under-18s.

title: UK GDPR privacy notice
why: A legal notice telling customers what we do with their personal details.

title: Website: Experiences page, prices, booking button, Gift Vouchers page, FAQ
why: Customers need a page to see the experiences and prices, and to buy.

title: Fix the outdated "coming to market in 2025" text and the placeholder launch news post
why: The website still says "coming to market in 2025", which looks out of date to customers.

title: Google Business Profile for the Dunmow base
why: Puts SmartMotion on Google Maps and search, with reviews and opening times.

title: Recheck prices against VR Sim
why: Make sure our prices make sense next to the nearest competitor before they're printed on vouchers.

title: Go-live gate: insurance certificate held, inspection date confirmed, licences signed, test purchase passed → open voucher sales and start the Christmas campaign
why: The final check that everything above is in place. Then switch on voucher sales for Christmas.

title: ADIPS design review, conformity, initial test; DOC issued
why: The official ride safety sign-off. No paying riders until we have it.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Operator training and written sign-off
why: Anyone running the rig is trained, and there's a written record that they're signed off.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Base fit-out: barrier, waiting area, spectator screen, ventilation
why: Getting the unit ready for customers: safety barrier, seating, a screen to watch, and fresh air.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: First-aider, AED plan, hygiene kit, incident log, RIDDOR procedure
why: First aid cover, a defibrillator plan, cleaning kit for headsets, and a way to record and report accidents.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Maintenance log, spares box, spare headset, backup PC image
why: Service records, plus spare parts and kit, so one breakdown doesn't cancel a day of bookings.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Staff and friends trial sessions; tune profiles for motion sickness
why: Practice sessions with friendly riders to fine-tune the motion and cut down motion sickness.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Event pack: insurance, DOC, risk assessment, power spec
why: The documents event organisers always ask for, ready to send in one go.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Book 2027 airshows and car shows
why: Get 2027 airshows and car shows in the diary.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Corporate target list (150 organisations within 60 miles), brochure, demo slots
why: A list of local companies to approach for team days, a brochure, and demo dates.
notes: Due date assumed: before the March 2027 public opening.

title: Simulator sales line: pricing, kit packages, design certification for buyers
why: Selling rigs to customers. On hold until the experiences business is running.

title: Custom SmartMotion flight game (SmartMotion Flight)
why: Our own flight experience, so we don't depend on game companies for paid rides. First version built; next steps are VR and motion-rig testing.
notes: v1 browser game built 9 Nov 2026; native Windows version (Godot 4.6, GPU, OpenXR for Quest 3, UDP telemetry) built the same day. Needs: test on the MSI laptop and Quest 3, connect the UDP feed to FlyPT Mover, check the Duxford layout, and settle the licence/insurance position for paid use.

title: 3D printing and design: build up the model library
why: Printed parts for the rig (button boxes, mounts, clips) and personal projects, designed and tracked in the Print & Design section.
notes: Print & Design section added 7 Nov 2026 with 3 starter models. Waiting for Sam's own models and design requests.

title: Second rig (when weekend utilisation stays above 75% for 3 months)
why: Only once weekends are consistently busy.

title: Bulldog DCS module or custom aircraft (ask Eagle Dynamics)
why: A marketing idea built around Skysmart's real Bulldog aircraft.
